title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Sports Rules and Strategy
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is an appropriate technique to emphasize to children who are practicing throwing a ball using an underhand throw?
options: releasing the ball at chest level on the throw
stopping the action of the follow through just after releasing the ball
beginning the throw with the side of the body facing the target
taking one step forward with the foot opposite the throwing hand
questions.explain: Stepping forward with the opposite foot (contralateral step) provides stability and transfers momentum forward, which is a key element for an effective and balanced underhand throw.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following techniques is most appropriate for players to keep in mind when dribbling a soccer ball?
options: alternating between the two feet in kicking the ball and keeping the eyes on the ball
moving at a speed faster than a walk and keeping the ball within two to four feet of the body
traveling in a zigzag pathway and keeping the ball directly below the head while moving
using a running motion to travel and delivering a series of taps to the ball with the foot
questions.explain: Effective soccer dribbling involves using a running motion while using soft, controlled taps to keep the ball close to the feet. This allows for better control and quick changes in direction while maintaining awareness of the field.

questions.q: For forehand and backhand volleys in tennis, which of the following techniques leads to a pivot on the back foot and a step toward the net, thus allowing a player to contact the ball in front of the body?
options: pointing the dominant elbow toward the opponent during the swing
bending the knees and keeping the back vertical
turning the shoulders early in preparation for the swing
rotating the racquet clockwise so the palm is on top of the racket
questions.explain: Turning the shoulders early initiates a 'unit turn,' where the body turns sideways. This movement naturally causes a pivot and allows the player to step into the volley and make contact with the ball in front of the body.

questions.q: During a backhand disc throw, keeping the back of the hand parallel with the ground and releasing the disc flat rather than at an angle are techniques used to:
options: generate an S-shaped pathway.
make the disc fly farther.
generate a sudden drop at the end of the flight.
make the disc skim the ground.
questions.explain: Releasing a disc flat and parallel to the ground ensures that the aerodynamic lift and momentum are directed forward, resulting in a straighter and longer flight path.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is a critical element of the ready position in badminton?
options: holding the racket down
standing with knees locked
holding the racket up
standing with weight on heels
questions.explain: In badminton's ready position, the player should hold the racket up and in front of the body. This allows for the quickest reaction to shots coming over the net. Knees should be bent and weight on the balls of the feet.

questions.q: Which of the following cues correctly describes a critical element of the two-handed side-arm strike used to bat a ball?
options: "Grip the bat so that your dominant hand is below your non-dominant hand."
"Transfer your weight from your back foot to your front foot as your hips and shoulder rotate into the swing."
"Hold the bat in front of your shoulder and keep your batting elbow perpendicular to the ground."
"Keep your batting elbow flexed during the entire swing and stop the follow-through at the point of contact."
questions.explain: A critical component of a powerful side-arm strike is kinetic chain sequencing. This involves transferring weight from the back foot to the front foot, initiated by hip and shoulder rotation, to generate maximum force.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental rule of field hockey and indoor floor hockey?
options: Follow-throughs may rise above waist level to chest height.
Players must keep only one hand on the stick at all times.
Excessive body contact or stick-to-stick contact is not allowed.
Players may kick or advance the ball or puck with any part of the body.
questions.explain: Both field hockey and floor hockey are not considered contact sports. To ensure safety, rules prohibit excessive body contact (like checking) and heavy stick-to-stick contact (like slashing).
